x: "Joe" King, one of our recent recruits, won the 10 miles Championship of the Southern Railway on February 8th.

Congratulations to Len Fletcher upon again winning the Surrey County Ten Miles Champioiship, and also to Joe King upon again winning the Sussex Twenty Miles Championship and beating the County record for the distance, which he held.
Green (6th), Joe King (not yet qualified as a team man, 7th), J.
Joe King was up from Brighton for the race and started well, but was obliged to retire at 12 miles through cramp, which attacked him after the 7th mile.
Then came Joe King (Ind. 34th) and Bob McMullen (36th), our fourth team man. Team scores were now Derby W.C. 47, Belgrave 67, Herne Hill H. 74, Surrey W.
Green won the Hastings to Brighton Walk, finishing 3½ miles ahead of the second man, Joe King, also of our Club.

Tommy Green, who only decided to come at 9 a.m. on the morning of the race, owing to a severe chill which had troubled him during the week, won the race by about a minute and a half from another Belgravian, Joe King.

Len Fletcher and Frank Elson have assisted the Club in seven of these eight wins ; Tommy Green six times ; Fred Rickards on three occasions ; Harold King, Frank Thorn and Ted Saunders each twice ; and Joe King and Jack Field once each.
Tommy Green went to the front at the start and at the end of the first mile led by a yard or two from Harold and Joe King, walking together, with Jack Field 80yds. behind.

Joe King was attacked by cramp, causing him to lose many places, and Rathbone also had to stop. Saunders from being our fifth man at 15 miles became our second man to finish and accomplished his best performance over twenty miles.
Joe King is also County Champion at 10 and 20 miles and was also first Sussex man to finish in the Hastings—Brighton Walk (38 miles), and must be acclaimed as a very versatile walker.
Joe King retired at this point, and Rickards, whose efforts over the Crawley—Bolney section now appeared to be taking their toll, eventually retired a few miles along the road.

Joe King walked probably his best "seven" yet and finished fourth, but our team again had to take second place to Enfield A.C. The performance of Harry Churcher, one of our individual entrants, in finishing sixth was very creditable, and he will assuredly be a tower of strength to our team in due course.

Over the last mile, Amer, a Surrey stalwart, made a gallant attempt to catch and pass Joe King. This would have given our Surrey friends victory by one point; but Joe, with an equally fine effort, held his position and in the final stages of the race was even getting away from his rival.
Neither has Joe King, although we hoped he would turn out for a race at the distance he likes best. As Fred Rickards had accomplished very fine performances in last year's 20 miles R.W.A.

The following Saturday (December 9th), Eastleigh Town S.C. are promoting a 12 miles Open Walk, and I should be glad to hear from members desirous of making the trip and supporting our "resident" members, Tommy Green and Joe King, in the team race.

Joe King was second man home, and with Bert Field completing the team, we were placed second in the scratch team race. Both scratch and team events went to the Surrey Walking Club, who had a very fine day out, for in addition they supplied first (H.
Martin and Joe King, both of whom will probably claim their team places. We shall have a really fit Fred Rickards, and in Frank Elson one who has regained his health and will be after his place.
Joe King, who had been placed third in the Sussex 20 Miles Championship, in fast time, the previous week, was an absentee, as were also two of our younger walkers, L.

Two points only separted us from the winners, Surrey Walking Club, at the conclusion of the race; and it was only natural that we should speculate on what would have happened if Tommy Green and Joe King had been able to make the journey.

Joe King, the Sussex Champion, then came into second position and so the race finished, with Don Brown never in any danger of being caught, although the time was fully three-quarters of a minute slower than his best.

Tommy Green and Joe King will be out whenever possible, Len Fletcher has been out training, Harry Churcher is now engaged in a business which gives him more time for training and racing than previously, Bill Treacher will soon be helping our teams on—in fact, all present and correct!
Last year we lost by a bare two points, but on this occasion we expect to have the help of both Tommy Green and Joe King, who were prevented from travelling to Sheffield last year.
In fact, it is rather surprising that we could still take second place, and this is due to some very fine walking by Joe King, sound work by the Bros.

A little farther back were Bentley, Bidgood, Rickards and Joe King, all walking together. It was as early as this that Jock Martin was having a struggle, suffering from a touch of sunstroke, but manfully keeping going.
We have two County Walking Champions in our ranks. Don Brown won the Surrey race, and Joe King the Sussex, both putting up fastest times.

Joe King, Jack Bidgood and others, striving their utmost. Of Harold King and Len Fletcher, and in more recent years, Harry Churcher winning the shorter distance road walks; supported by as fine a bunch of sportsmen as ever stepped into racing kit.
Has had " a few " with Tommy Green, and met an old Belgravian in Joe King. He proposes to start a Hampshire section (like Cadogan), with Green Junior and Senior, King, Clayton.
